evidence.source_sentence: Poly(styrene-co-acrylic acid) [P(S-co-AA)] copolymers were prepared by the free-radical bulk copolymerization of purified styrene and acrylic acid monomers with benzoyl peroxide as the initiator.

To neutralize the acid groups, a predetermined amount of methanolic NaOH and CsOH was added to the P(S-co-AA) samples in a benzene/methanol (9/1 v/v) mixture, which gave Na- and Cs-neutralized poly(styrene-co-acrylate) ionomers—P(S-co-ANa) and P(S-co-ACs)—respectively.

The $\gamma _ { \mathrm { s } }$values for the PS homopolymer and acid copolymer containing 6.6 mol % of acid groups, P(S-6.6-AA), initially increase significantly upon PSII treatment and then decrease with aging time.

In the case of the 6.6 mol $\%$ionomers, that is, P(S-6.6-ANa) and P(S-6.6-ACs), the PSII treatment increases the $\gamma _ { \mathrm { s } }$values, especially $\gamma _ { \mathrm { s } } ^ { \mathrm { p } }$values, drastically, and the $\gamma _ { \mathrm { s } }$values do not change significantly with aging time.

The strength of ionic interactions in multiplets is one of the useful factors for explaining the results that the modified surfaces of P(S-6.6-ANa) and P(S-6.6-ACs) ionomers are more stable than those of the P(S-6.6-AA) copolymers.

To make thin polymer films, 7 wt % ionomer–tetrahydrofuran solutions were deposited onto a disposable aluminum dish.

The polymer samples were placed on the oil-cooled stage surrounded by the plasma and biased to a high negative potential of -5 kV with a pulse width of 10 $\mu \mathbf { s }$at a pulse repetition of 500 Hz.

To make thin polymer films, 7 wt % ionomer–tetrahydrofuran solutions were deposited onto a disposable aluminum dish. The solvent was allowed to evaporate slowly for about 5 days. Subsequently, thin-film samples were dried further in vacuo at room temperature for 12 h.

The $\mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$plasma was generated at a pressure of 1 mTorr and with an r.f. power of 200 W. The polymer samples were placed on the oil-cooled stage surrounded by the plasma and biased to a high negative potential of -5 kV with a pulse width of 10 $\mu \mathbf { s }$at a pulse repetition of 500 Hz. The PSII treatment time was 1 min.
